reasons: Both answers open by correcting both false premises (replacement in Guangzhou, and 12306 e-certificate or station paper certificate for boarding). Both give the correct 40 yuan fee, 10 yuan temporary ID and the 24-hour, 6-per-month limit. A gives more policy specifics (2017 nationwide rollout), answers the hometown case directly, and avoids making the hukou book mandatory. But it is longer and repetitive, contradicts itself on simultaneous temporary-ID application, says 'on the spot or within 3 days' for a hometown temporary ID, and has one broken citation link. B is tighter and gets the temporary-ID timing right (about 5 working days after Henan police issue it, too tight for Oct 30-31). But it calls the hukou book the 'most critical' document and tells the user to courier it, which is a listed key trap, and its 'mid-to-late November' estimate conflicts with its own 40-day figure. The two are close, with A slightly ahead on the trap and specifics and B slightly ahead on concision and temporary-ID timing.
